subject: CoreAI production throttles — reconciliation, short-term mitigation, and credit proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@coreai.com>, SRE Team <sre@coreai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CoreAI production throttles — immediate mitigation and next steps

Hi Daniel / CoreAI SRE team,

Thanks for flagging the increase in 429s this morning. We tracked the first spikes at ~09:00 PST and saw error rates concentrated on requests that exceeded a recent tenant-rate mapping change we rolled last week.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Reverted the tenant-rate mapping rollback for CoreAI to the previous profile (effective 09:05 PST).
- Applied a short-term per-API-instance cap to smooth bursts while we reconcile historical token patterns.
- Enabled verbose request logging for the affected tenant; attached is a CSV of sampled throttled request headers (throttle_logs_0329.csv).

Impact we understand so far:
- ~12% of token requests returned 429 over a 40-minute window (affecting ingestion and model-serve endpoints).
- Latency increased for a subset of batched requests while the system rebalanced.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We will open a joint call at 11:00 PST to walk through the logs and confirm recovery metrics. Please confirm availability.
2) We'll draft a post-incident note and a proposed one-time credit for the affected window; sharing a draft this afternoon.
3) Marcus will lead a technical root-cause investigation and share a remediation checklist — expected in 48 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize clarity on root cause and credits.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: throttle_logs_0329.csv (sampled request headers)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@coreai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@coreai.com>, Procurement <procure@coreai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreAI production throttles — immediate mitigation and next steps

Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick response and for reverting the mapping — things already look better from our side, but we're still seeing intermittent 429s impacting the inference pipeline (batch jobs are failing intermittently which triggers retries upstream).

Here are two immediate asks from us:
- Can you confirm the exact time window you used to calculate the one-time credit and the formula? Procurement will need that for audit.
- For the joint call, we'll include our SRE lead (K. Lim) and the person who owns batching logic on our side.

We're available for the 11:00 PST call.

On the logs — we'll share a snippet of our error traces during the call. Appreciate the transparency here.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Director of Platform Engineering, CoreAI
daniel.park@coreai.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreAI production throttles — immediate mitigation and next steps

Daniel / team,

Quick technical update from our side after initial log review: the tenant-rate mapping change introduced an unintended translation of per-tenant burst tokens into a stricter per-API-instance ceiling. That mismatch is what produced the unexpected 429s once overlapping short-lived bursts occurred.

Short-term fixes applied (already active):
- Rollback (09:05 PST) reverted per-tenant burst allowances.
- Temporary instance-level smoothing applied to avoid synchronized throttle resets.

Follow-up remediation we will take over the next 48 hrs:
- Reconcile historical token distribution and create a new mapping rule that preserves burst allowances while enforcing steady-state limits.
- Add unit and integration tests to prevent mapping regressions during rollout.
- Add metric alarms that track per-tenant burst vs instance ceilings so automated rollouts are gated.

I've attached a sampled log export (throttle_logs_0329.csv) and included inline examples below. If you can share traces for the failed batch job, that will speed correlation.

Marcus Lin
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreAI production throttles — immediate mitigation and next steps

Thanks, Marcus and Daniel.

Daniel — attaching a draft post-incident note that outlines the timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation we applied, and our proposed one-time credit calculation (redwood_postmortem_draft_CoreAI.docx). High level on credits: we propose a pro-rated credit equal to the estimated affected token volume times the standard hosted rate for the duration of the incident window (09:00–09:40 PST). We'll include an audit-ready CSV of the affected requests as part of the postmortem packet.

Planned timeline:
- Draft postmortem out for your review this afternoon (EOD).
- Technical RCA and remediation checklist from Marcus by end of day Wed (48 hrs).
- Formal postmortem and final credit amount by next Friday.

Would you like us to include a short (15–20m) executive readout for procurement and your leadership when we finalize? We can schedule for next week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_draft_CoreAI.docx

Hi Daniel —

Thank you again for collaborating on the call yesterday. Quick summary and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of impact:
- Incident window: 2027-03-29T09:00:00-07:00 to 2027-03-29T09:40:00-07:00.
- Peak 429 rate: ~12% of token requests; primarily affected batch ingestion.

Agreed next steps:
1) Marcus to deliver a technical RCA and remediation checklist by EOD Wed (2027-03-31).
2) Stephanie to finalize postmortem and proposed credit; expected by EOD Mon (2027-04-04).
3) Scheduling: 15m executive readout for Procurement + CoreAI leadership; proposed window: Tue 2027-04-05 10:00 PST — please confirm. HubSpot deal updated: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/48290

Credit approach: pro-rated token-based credit for the affected window (detailed in the draft). If procurement requires alternate billing offsets, let us know and we'll coordinate.

If you'd like, we can also provide an engineering walkthrough of the new mapping unit tests once they're merged.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
